abstract: We identify the Bethe algebra of the Gaudin model associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {gl}_N$</tex> acting on a suitable representation with the center of the rational Cherednik algebra at the critical level and with the algebra of regular functions on the Calogero–Moser space.

articleTitle: Errata and Addenda to “Odds and Ends on Finite Group Actions and Traces”
abstract: We wish to correct a few typographical errors in [3], and take the opportunity to point out a few additional consequences of [3] on fixed-point sets of finite group actions and complement some results of Esnault and Nicaise [2] in the case of affine spaces.

articleTitle: On the Laplace Transform for Tempered Holomorphic Functions
abstract: In order to discuss the Fourier-Sato transform of not necessarily conic sheaves, we compensate the lack of homogeneity by adding an extra variable. We can then obtain Paley–Wiener-type results, using a theorem by Kashiwara and Schapira on the Laplace transform for tempered holomorphic functions. As a key tool in our approach, we introduce the subanalytic sheaf of holomorphic functions with exponential growth, which should be of independent interest.

articleTitle: Rieffel Deformation and Twisted Crossed Products
abstract: To a continuous action of a vector group on a C*-algebra, twisted by the imaginary exponential of a symplectic form, one associates a Rieffel deformed algebra as well as a twisted crossed product. We show that the second one is isomorphic to the tensor product of the first one with the C*-algebra of compact operators in a separable Hilbert space and we indicate some applications.

articleTitle: Positive Representations of Split Real Quantum Groups and Future Perspectives
abstract: We construct a special principal series representation for the modular double <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{{\mathfrak q} \bar {\mathfrak q}}(\mathfrak g\mathbb R)$</tex> of type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> representing the generators by positive essentially self-adjoint operators satisfying the transcendental relations that also relate q and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde q$</tex>. We use the cluster variables parameterization of the positive unipotent matrices to derive the formulas in the classical case. Then we quantize them after applying the Mellin transform. Our construction is inspired by the previous results for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R}=\mathfrak {sl}(2,\mathbb R)$</tex> and can be generalized to all other types of simple split real Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R}$</tex>. We conjecture that our positive representations are closed under the tensor product and we discuss the future perspectives of the new representation theory following the parallel with the established developments of the finite-dimensional representation theory of quantum groups.

articleTitle: Main Conjectures for CM Fields and a Yager-Type Theorem for Rubin–Stark Elements
abstract: In this article, we study the p-ordinary Iwasawa theory of the (conjectural) Rubin–Stark elements defined over abelian extensions of a CM field F and develop a rank-g Euler–Kolyvagin system machinery (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2g=[F:\mathbb Q]$</tex>), refining and generalizing Perrin-Riou's theory and the author's prior work. This has several important arithmetic consequences: using the recent results of Hida and Hsieh on the CM main conjectures, we prove a natural extension of a theorem of Yager for the CM field F, where we relate the Rubin–Stark elements to the several-variable Katz p-adic L-function. Furthermore, beyond the cases covered by Hida and Hsieh, we are able to reduce the p-ordinary CM main conjectures to a local statement about the Rubin–Stark elements. We discuss applications of our results in the arithmetic of CM abelian varieties.

articleTitle: ADE Bundles over Surfaces with ADE Singularities
abstract: Given a compact complex surface X with an ADE singularity and p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>=0, we construct ADE bundles over X and its minimal resolution Y. Furthermore, we describe their minuscule representation bundles in terms of configurations of (reducible) (−1)-curves in Y.

articleTitle: Linear Independence of Knots Arising from Iterated Infection Without the Use of Tristram–Levine Signature
abstract: We give an explicit construction of linearly independent families of knots arbitrarily deep in the (n)-solvable filtration of the knot concordance group using a metabelian ρ-invariant. A difference between previous constructions of infinite rank subgroups in the concordance group and ours is that the deepest infecting knots in the construction we present are allowed to have vanishing Tristram–Levine signatures.

articleTitle: On Linnik's Conjecture: Sums of Squares and Microsquares
abstract: We show that almost all natural numbers n not divisible by 4, and not congruent to 7 modulo 8, are represented as the sum of three squares, one of which is the square of an integer no larger than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\log n)^{1+\varepsilon}$</tex>. This answers a conjecture of Linnik for almost all natural numbers, and sharpens a conclusion of Bourgain, Rudnick, and Sarnak concerning nearest neighbor distances between normalized integral points on the sphere.

articleTitle: Group Structures of Elliptic Curves Over Finite Fields
abstract: It is well known that if E is an elliptic curve over the finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_p$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E(\mathbb F_p)\simeq \mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z \times \mathbb Z/mk\mathbb Z$</tex> for some positive integers m,k. Let S(M,K) denote the set of pairs (m,k) with m≤M and k≤K for which there exists an elliptic curve over some prime finite field whose group of points is isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z \times \mathbb Z/mk\mathbb Z$</tex>. Banks, Pappalardi, and Shparlinski recently conjectured that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\leq(\log M)^{2-\in}$</tex>, then a density zero proportion of the groups in question actually arises as the group of points on some elliptic curve over some prime finite field. On the other hand, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\geq(\log M)^{2+\in}$</tex>, they conjectured that a density 1 proportion of the groups in question arises as the group of points on some elliptic curve over some prime finite field. We prove that the first part of their conjecture holds in the full range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\leq(\log M)^{2-\in}$</tex>, and we prove that the second part of their conjecture holds in the limited range K≥M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+ϵ</sup>. In the wider range K≥M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, we show that at least a positive density of the groups in question actually occurs.

articleTitle: Weil's Converse Theorem with Poles
abstract: We prove a generalization of the classical converse theorem of Weil, allowing the twists by nontrivial Dirichlet characters to have arbitrary poles.

articleTitle: Calderón–Zygmund Operators Associated to Matrix-Valued Kernels
abstract: Calderón–Zygmund operators with noncommuting kernels may fail to be L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>-bounded for p≠2, even for kernels with good size/smoothness properties. In this paper, we obtain weak-type estimates for perfect dyadic CZO’s and cancellative Haar shifts associated to noncommuting kernels in terms of a row/column decomposition of the function. General CZO’s satisfy analogous H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>→L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> type estimates. In conjunction with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty}\rightarrow{\rm BMO}$</tex> type estimates, we get similar row/column L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> estimates. Our approach also applies to paraproducts/martingale transforms with noncommuting symbols.

articleTitle: L4-Norms of the Dihedral Maass Forms
abstract: In this paper, we prove the optimal bound for L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>-norms of the dihedral Maass forms associated to Hecke’s grossencharacters of a fixed real quadratic field, as their Laplacian eigenvalues tend to infinity.

articleTitle: Koszul Duality and Mixed Hodge Modules
abstract: We prove that on a certain class of smooth complex varieties (those with “affine even stratifications”), the category of mixed Hodge modules is “almost” Koszul: it becomes Koszul after a few unwanted extensions are eliminated. We also give an equivalence between perverse sheaves on such a variety and modules for a certain graded ring, obtaining a formality result as a corollary. For flag varieties, these results were proved earlier by Beilinson–Ginzburg–Soergel using a rather different construction.

articleTitle: Rational Curves on $\bar M_g$ and K3 Surfaces
abstract: Let (S,L) be a smooth primitively polarized K3 surface of genus g and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:X\rightarrow\mathbb P^1$</tex> be the fibration defined by a linear pencil in |L|. For f general and g≥7, we work out the splitting type of the locally free sheaf <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi^*_fT_{\bar M_g}$</tex>, where Ψ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> is the modular morphism associated to f. We show that this splitting type encodes the fundamental geometrical information attached to Mukai’s projection map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal P_g\rightarrow\bar {\mathcal M_g}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal P_g$</tex> is the stack parameterizing pairs (S,C) with (S,L) as above and C∈|L| a stable curve. Moreover, we work out conditions on a fibration f to induce a modular morphism Ψ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> such that the normal sheaf N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ψf</inf> is locally free.

articleTitle: Joseph Ideals and Harmonic Analysis for $\mathfrak {osp}(m|2n)$
abstract: The Joseph ideal in the universal enveloping algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal U(\mathfrak so(m))$</tex> is the annihilator ideal of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {so}(m)$</tex>-representation on the harmonic functions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^{m-2}$</tex>. The Joseph ideal for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {sp}(2n)$</tex> is the annihilator ideal of the Segal–Shale–Weil (metaplectic) representation. Both ideals can be constructed in a unified way from a quadratic relation in the tensor algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\otimes \mathfrak g$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {so}(m)$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {sp}(2n)$</tex>. In this paper, we construct two analogous ideals in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\otimes \mathfrak g$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal U(\mathfrak g)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> the orthosymplectic Lie super-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {osp}(m|2n)=\mathfrak {spo}(2n|m)$</tex> and prove that they have unique characterizations that naturally extend the classical case. Then we show that these two ideals are the annihilator ideals of, respectively, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {osp}(m|2n)$</tex>-representation on the spherical harmonics on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^{m-2|2n}$</tex> and a generalization of the metaplectic representation to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {spo}(2n|m)$</tex>. This proves that these ideals are reasonable candidates to establish the theory of Joseph-like ideals for Lie super-algebras. We also discuss the relation between the Joseph ideal of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {spo}(2n|m)$</tex> and the algebra of symmetries of the super-conformal Laplace operator, regarded as an intertwining operator between principal series representations for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {spo}(2n|m)$</tex>. As a side result, we obtain the proof of a conjecture of Eastwood about the Cartan product of irreducible representations of semisimple Lie algebras made in [10].

articleTitle: A Sum–Product Theorem in Function Fields
abstract: Let A be a finite subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_q((t^{-1}))$</tex>, the field of Laurent series in 1/t over a finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_q$</tex>. We show that, for any ϵ>0, there exists a constant C dependent only on ϵ and q such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\max\{|A+A|,|AA|\}\geq C|A|^{6/5-\in}$</tex>. In particular, such a result is obtained for the rational function field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_q(t)$</tex>. Identical results are also obtained for finite subsets of the p-adic field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q_p$</tex> for any prime p.

articleTitle: A Theorem of Roe and Strichartz for Riemannian Symmetric Spaces of Noncompact Type
abstract: Generalizing a result of Roe [14], Strichartz proved in [16] that if a doubly infinite sequence {f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>} of functions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^n$</tex> satisfies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k+1</inf>=Δf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> and |f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>(x)|≤M for all k=0,±1,±2,… and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\in \mathbb R^n$</tex>, then Δf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(x)=−f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Strichartz also showed that the result fails for hyperbolic 3-space. This negative result can indeed be extended to any Riemannian symmetric space of noncompact type. Taking this into account, we shall prove that for all Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type the theorem actually holds true when uniform boundedness is modified suitably.

articleTitle: The Reciprocity Conjecture of Khare and Wintenberger
abstract: We prove a strengthening of the “reciprocity conjecture” of Khare and Wintenberger. The input to the original conjecture is an odd prime p, a CM number field F containing the pth roots of unity, and a pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak q_1,\mathfrak q_2)$</tex> of primes of the maximal totally real subfield F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> of F that are inert in the cyclotomic Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>-extension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F^+_{\infty}/F^+$</tex>. In analogy to a statement about generalized Jacobians of curves, the conjecture asserts the equality of two procyclic subgroups of the Galois group of the maximal pro-p extension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal M$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F^+_{\infty}$</tex> that is unramified outside p and abelian over F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. The first is the intersection with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gal}(\mathcal M/F^+_{\infty})$</tex> of the closed subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gal}(\mathcal M/F^+)$</tex> generated by the Frobenius elements of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak q_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak q_2$</tex>. The second is generated by the class of an exact sequence defining the minus part of the p-part of the ray class group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_{\infty}$</tex> of conductor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak q_1,\mathfrak q_2)$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Ginibre Ensemble and Gaussian Analytic Functions
abstract: We show that as n changes, the characteristic polynomial of the n×n random matrix with i.i.d. complex Gaussian entries can be described recursively through a process analogous to Pólya’s urn scheme. As a result, we get a random analytic function in the limit, which is given by a mixture of Gaussian analytic functions. This suggests another reason why the zeros of Gaussian analytic functions and the Ginibre ensemble exhibit similar local repulsion, but different global behavior. Our approach gives new explicit formulas for the limiting analytic function.

articleTitle: Variétés CR polarisées et G-polarisées, partie I
abstract: Polarized and G-polarized CR manifolds are smooth manifolds endowed with a double structure: a real foliation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex> (given by the action of a Lie group G in the G-polarized case) and a transverse CR distribution (E,J). Polarized means that (E,J) is roughly speaking invariant by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex>. Both structures are therefore linked up. The interplay between them gives to polarized CR-manifolds a very rich geometry. In this paper, we study the properties of polarized and G-polarized manifolds, putting special emphasis on the existence of a local moduli space.

articleTitle: Picard Bundles and Brill–Noether Loci in the Compactified Jacobian of a Nodal Curve
abstract: Let X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> denote an irreducible projective nodal curve with k nodes and of genus g(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>). We prove a generalization of the classical Poincaré formula to the compactified Jacobian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar J^0(X_k)$</tex> the moduli space of torsion-free sheaves of rank 1 and degree 0 on X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>. We apply it to show that the Brill–Noether loci are nonempty if the Brill–Noether number is nonnegative. We prove that for d≥2g(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>), the Picard bundle on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar J^0(X_k)$</tex> is stable but not ample, unlike in the case of a smooth curve. However, for the pullback of the Picard bundle to the desingularization of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar J^d(X_k)$</tex>, the restriction to a general complete intersection subvariety of codimension k is ample. We use this to show that the Brill–Noether loci are connected if the Brill–Noether number is bigger than k. We prove that the Picard bundle is semistable for d=2g(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>)−1.

articleTitle: Interpolation, Box Splines, and Lattice Points in Zonotopes
abstract: Let X be a totally unimodular list of vectors in some lattice. Let B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> be the box spline defined by X. Its support is the zonotope Z(X). We show that any real-valued function defined on the set of lattice points in the interior of Z(X) can be extended to a function on Z(X) of the form p(D)B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> in a unique way, where p(D) is a differential operator that is contained in the so-called internal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal P$</tex>-space. This was conjectured by Olga Holtz and Amos Ron. We also point out connections between this interpolation problem and matroid theory, including a deletion-contraction decomposition.

articleTitle: Periods of Saito–Kurokawa Representations
abstract: Suppose that Π is an irreducible unitary automorphic representation in the discreet spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm SO}(3,2)_\mathbb A$</tex> and Π<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup> an irreducible cuspidal unitary representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm GSO}_4(\mathbb A)$</tex>. When Π is in the Saito–Kurokawa packet, we show that the square of the global SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-period of Π⊗Π<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>, when nonvanishing, is a product of local periods defined by regularized integrals of matrix coefficients.

articleTitle: A Sharp Bilinear Estimate for the Klein–Gordon Equation in ℝ1+1
abstract: We prove a sharp bilinear estimate for the one-dimensional Klein–Gordon equation. The proof involves an unlikely combination of five trigonometric identities. We also prove new estimates for the restriction of the Fourier transform to the hyperbola, where the pullback measure is not assumed to be compactly supported.

articleTitle: Inductive Approach to Effective b-Semiampleness
abstract: An lc-trivial fibration is the data of a pair (X,B) and a fibration such that (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>+B)|<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> is torsion where F is the general fiber. For such a fibration, we have an equality K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>+B+1/r(φ)=f*(K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>+B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>+M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>), where B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf> is the discriminant of f, M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf> is the moduli part, and φ is a rational function. It has been conjectured by Prokhorov and Shokurov that there exists an integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m=m(r,\dim\ F)$</tex> such that mM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z′</inf> is base-point-free on some birational model Z′ of Z. In this work, we reduce this conjecture to the case where the base Z has dimension 1. Moreover, in the case, where M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>≡0, we prove the existence of an integer m that depends only on the middle Betti number of a canonical covering of the fiber, such that mM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>∼0.

articleTitle: Moments of L′(½) in the Family of Quadratic Twists
abstract: We prove the asymptotic formulae for several moments of derivatives of GL(2) L-functions over quadratic twists. The family of L-functions we consider has root number fixed to −1 and odd orthogonal symmetry. Assuming generalized Riemann hypothesis, we prove the asymptotic formulae for (1) the second moment with one secondary term, (2) the moment of two distinct modular forms f and g, and (3) the first moment with controlled weight and level dependence. We also include some immediate corollaries to elliptic curves using the modularity theorem and the work of Gross and Zagier.

articleTitle: Strong and Weak Type Estimates for Singular Integrals with Respect to Measures Separated by AD-regular Boundaries
abstract: We prove weak and strong boundedness estimates for singular integrals in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^d$</tex> with respect to (d−1)-dimensional measures separated by Ahlfors–David regular boundaries, generalizing and extending results of Chousionis and Mattila. Our proof follows a different strategy based on new Calderón–Zygmund decompositions which can also be used to extend a result of David.

articleTitle: Existence of Generalized Totally Umbilic 2-Spheres in Perturbed 3-Spheres
abstract: It was recently shown by Souam and Toubiana [34] that the (nonconstantly curved) Berger spheres do not contain totally umbilic surfaces. Nevertheless, in this article we show, by perturbative arguments, that all analytic metrics sufficiently close to the round metric g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb S^3$</tex> possess generalized totally umbilic 2-spheres, namely critical points of the conformal Willmore functional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int_\Sigma|A^\circ|^2\ {\mathrm d}\mu_\gamma$</tex>. The same is true in the smooth setting provided a suitable nondegeneracy condition on the traceless Ricci tensor holds. The proof involves a gluing process of two different finite-dimensional reduction schemes, a sharp asymptotic analysis of the functional on perturbed umbilic spheres of small radius and a quantitative Schur-type Lemma in order to treat the cases when the traceless Ricci tensor of the perturbation is degenerate but not identically zero. For left-invariant metrics on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm SU}(2)\cong\mathbb S^3$</tex>, our result implies the existence of uncountably many distinct Willmore spheres.

articleTitle: Some Higher Order Isoperimetric Inequalities via the Method of Optimal Transport
abstract: In this paper, we establish some sharp inequalities between the volume and the integral of the kth mean curvature for (k+1)-convex domains in the Euclidean space. The results generalize the classical Alexandrov–Fenchel inequalities for convex domains. Our proof utilizes the method of optimal transportation.

articleTitle: Further Unifying Two Approaches to the Hyperplane Conjecture
abstract: We compare and combine two approaches that have been recently introduced by Dafnis and Paouris [7] and by Klartag and Milman [13] with the aim of providing bounds for the isotropic constants of convex bodies. By defining a new hereditary parameter for all isotropic logarithmically concave measures, we are able to show that the method in [13], and the apparently stronger conclusions it leads to, can be extended in the full range of the “weaker” assumptions of Dafnis and Paouris [7]. The new parameter we define is related to the highest dimension k≤n−1 in which one can always find marginals of an n-dimensional isotropic log-concave measure that have bounded isotropic constant.

articleTitle: Triangular Bases in Quantum Cluster Algebras
abstract: A lot of recent activity has been directed toward various constructions of “natural” bases in cluster algebras. We develop a new approach to this problem which is close in spirit to Lusztig's construction of a canonical basis, and the pioneering construction of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis in a Hecke algebra. The key ingredient of our approach is a new version of Lusztig's Lemma that we apply to all acyclic quantum cluster algebras. As a result, we construct the “canonical” basis in every such algebra that we call the canonical triangular basis.

articleTitle: Hilbert Schemes as Moduli of Higgs Bundles and Local Systems
abstract: We construct five families of 2D moduli spaces of parabolic Higgs bundles (respectively, local systems) by taking the equivariant Hilbert scheme of a certain finite group acting on the cotangent bundle of an elliptic curve (respectively, twisted cotangent bundle). We show that the Hilbert scheme of m points of these surfaces is again a moduli space of parabolic Higgs bundles (respectively, local systems), confirming a conjecture of Boalch in these cases and extending a result of Gorsky–Nekrasov–Rubtsov. Using the McKay correspondence, we establish the autoduality conjecture for the derived categories of the moduli spaces of Higgs bundles under consideration.
